basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 1-6.' and it opens 'VERS. 1-6.--Deinde sequitur qualiter reges gentium percusserunt Raphaim in'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 1-6.--Deinde sequitur qualiter reges gentium percusserunt Raphaim in Astarothcarnaim quoque, et Zozim cum eis, et reliqua. Raphaim gigantes interpretantur; Zozim, terribiles et horrendi; Astaroth civitas, quae usque hodie sic vocatur, significat quod quatuor reges interfecerunt gigantes, et robustos quoque Arabiae; Astarothcarnaim, terram gigantum quamdam in supercilio Sodomorum.
